# Routes, content model, and future API contract

> **Revised for Astro** (supersedes the earlier NestJS-controller-based routing section
> of this file — the content model further below is unchanged).

## Pages (statically generated by Astro)

| Route | File | Replaces (from source HTML) |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `src/pages/index.astro` | `#view-home` — sidebar + hero + about + experience + education + certifications + skills + projects + articles + languages + recommendations + connect + footer |
| `/projects/:slug` | `src/pages/projects/[slug].astro` (via `getStaticPaths()` over the `projects` collection) | `#view-case-study` (currently only `beyondrxaid`) |
| `/articles/:slug` | `src/pages/articles/[slug].astro` (via `getStaticPaths()` over the `articles` collection) | `#view-article` (currently only `clean-architecture-in-dotnet`) |

All three are pre-rendered HTML at build time — no server needed to serve them.
Anchor nav (`About`, `Experience`, `Education`, `Skills`) is plain `<a href="/#about">`
etc., using normal navigation + browser anchor scroll — no JS required (the original's
`goHomeAndScroll()`/`showView()` JS hack isn't needed once these are real static routes
instead of hidden divs).

## Future API contract (not built yet — documented now so phase 2 has a target)

When the separate API service is built later, these are the endpoints the two dynamic
islands (`FeedbackButtons`, `CommentForm`) will call, and what any future consumer of
this content would use:

| Method & path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/profile` | name, role, blurb, facts, socials, email, cv link |
| `GET /api/experience` | timeline entries |
| `GET /api/education` | education entries |
| `GET /api/certifications` | certification entries |
| `GET /api/skills` | key skills + full skill tags + tool badges |
| `GET /api/projects` | project list (cards) |
| `GET /api/projects/:slug` | full case-study detail |
| `GET /api/articles` | article list (cards) |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug` | full article detail (body, code blocks, reaction counts) |
| `POST /api/articles/:slug/reaction` | body `{ type: 'like' \| 'dislike' }` → replaces `toggleFeedback()`, persists |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug/comments` | comment list for an article |
| `POST /api/articles/:slug/comments` | body `{ name, email?, comment }` → replaces `submitComment()`, persists |
| `GET /api/languages` | languages + proficiency |
| `GET /api/recommendations` | recommendation entries |

In phase 1, `FeedbackButtons` and `CommentForm` implement their **static** behavior
(in-browser only, matching the original file exactly) without calling any of this. In
phase 2, they read `PUBLIC_API_URL` and call the `reaction`/`comments` endpoints above —
a contained edit, not a rewrite.

## Content model (extracted from the source HTML — this becomes the shared DTOs/interfaces in `modules/content`)

- **Profile**: `name`, `role`, `blurb`, `avatarInitials`, `facts: string[]`, `socials: { github, linkedin, x }`, `email`, `cvUrl`
- **Experience**: `title`, `company`, `employmentType`, `startDate`, `endDate | 'Present'`, `description`, `bullets: string[]`
- **Education**: `degree`, `institution`, `description`, `dateRange` — *placeholder data in source, needs real content*
- **Certification**: `name`, `issuer`, `issuedDate`, `url?` — *placeholder data in source*
- **Skills**: `keySkills: string[]` (About section badges), `fullSkills: string[]` (Skills section badges), `tools: { code, label }[]` (short-code badges)
- **Project**: `name`, `dateRange`, `description`, `tags: string[]`, `slug?`, `hasCaseStudy: boolean`; when `hasCaseStudy` — `role, timeline, stack, category, architecture: { label, sublabel }[], overview, contributions: { title, points: string[] }[], beforeAfter: { aspect, before, after }[], prevProjectLabel, nextProjectLabel`
- **Article**: `title`, `date`, `excerpt`, `slug?`, `hasFullPost: boolean`; when `hasFullPost` — `readTime, sections: { heading, body, quote?: {text, cite}, code?: {lang, code} }[], likeCount, dislikeCount`
- **Language**: `name`, `proficiency` — one real (English), one placeholder in source
- **Recommendation**: `recommenderName`, `role`, `quote` — *placeholder data in source, both entries*
- **Comment**: `articleSlug`, `name`, `email?`, `comment`, `createdAt`, `isAuthor`, `parentId?` (for the one reply thread shown)

Note: several sections in the source HTML are explicitly marked
`<!-- placeholder — no source data provided -->` (Education, Certifications,
Recommendations, second Language entry). The NestJS port keeps these as real,
editable seed records (not hardcoded template text) so filling them in later is a data
edit, not a template edit.
